title: Failure Prediction at Runtime for Generative Robot Policies
models: single-task diffusion policy (DDPM, temporal U-Net, ResNet-18 encoder) for PushT, Pretzel, PushChair
single-task flow-matching policy with ACT transformer backbone for Sorting and Stacking
action_head: diffusion policy / flow matching (not a VLA)
methods: random network distillation in the policy's frozen observation-embedding space (RND-OE)
action-chunk entropy (ACE) via dimension-wise binning over a batch of sampled chunks in end-effector space
functional conformal prediction thresholds; AND-combination of the two predictors
question: Can failures of generative imitation policies be predicted early, without failure data, by requiring both out-of-distribution observation embeddings and high entropy of sampled action chunks?
key_findings: Averaged over five environments (Table 1, 5 seeds): FIPER TWA 0.65, balanced accuracy 0.78, detection time 0.30 vs best baseline logpZO 0.60 / 0.69 / 0.35 and STAC 0.57 / 0.68 / 0.42; overall TPR 0.92.
Per task FIPER is not always best: Stacking PCA-kmeans TWA 0.66 vs FIPER 0.62; PushT STAC 0.58 vs 0.55; Pretzel ACE alone 0.75 vs FIPER 0.68.

RND-OE and ACE separate 'success under OOD' from 'failure in distribution' better than the other observation- and action-based scores (Fig. 4); action-based scores separate fail from success less than observation-based ones.
AND-combination with a time-varying threshold gives TPR 0.91 / TNR 0.65; OR-combination gives TPR 1.00 but TNR 0.05 (Table 2).
Cumulative scores (as in STAC) mostly detect failures because failed rollouts are longer; single-timestep scores (as in FAIL-Detect logpZO) give many false alarms (Figs. 5-6).
ACE beats STAC especially on tasks with discrete action multimodality (Sorting, Stacking, Pretzel), because variance-style consistency flags mode switches as uncertainty.

evidence.scale: M = 50 successful calibration rollouts in simulation, M = 10 in real tasks; test rollout counts in an appendix table (not extracted); 5 seeds; results averaged over calibration quantiles 0.90-0.99
evidence.statistics: partial: mean +/- std over 5 seeds (many std are 0.00, implying seeds vary detector training rather than rollouts); no tests

causal_validation: None; uncertainty and novelty scores only.
closed_loop: Offline evaluation on recorded rollouts; no intervention.
limitations_stated: Needs a set of successful rollouts and a separately trained RND model.
Runtime cost could grow for very high-dimensional action spaces (e.g. humanoids).
Only single-task vision-based imitation policies; adapting to large VLAs is future work.
critique: Not a VLA paper: single-task diffusion/flow policies with ResNet-18 encoders, so its success says little about VLA internals; it is in this batch as the main non-probe baseline (FIPER) used by GUARD, Tri-Info and VLA-Scope.
Window size and threshold type are selected per method as the values maximizing TWA across all environments, i.e. tuned on the test environments.
ACE needs a batch of sampled action chunks each step, which later VLA papers (SAFE, VLA-FAIL) argue is too expensive for large VLAs.
Important methodological warning for the review: cumulative failure scores largely reflect that failed episodes run longer, a shortcut that several VLA failure papers must guard against.
Seed std of 0.00 on most entries means variability across independent rollouts is not measured.
one_line: FIPER flags failures of diffusion and flow-matching imitation policies, without failure data, when both a novelty score on the policy's observation embedding and the entropy of sampled action chunks stay high over a short window, beating OOD and consistency baselines on five tasks.
